More on happiness and the meaning of life.

So, what would the meaning of life be for TK?

"The meaning of life is to increase fitness." Evolutionary
Psychology people (the field that Robert Wright surveys in
his book "The Moral Animal") would extend this slightly with
"Collective Fitness Theory" (I think this is the name...
close at least...)

namely:

"The meaning of life is to increase *collective* fitness."
As in... you and those you are related to.  Kinship.  To heck
with the rest of the world.  Selfishness.

TK was very selfish.  He was projecting his world-view onto
everyone else.

"Is the Bomber a would-be writer who mails bombs to get
editors to print his work? Or does he want editors to print
his work so people can understand why he mails the bombs? He
says he's not into politics, so he must be into writing.  Bad
writers need bombs."
http://www.thenation.com/issue/950918/column.htm
   
According to interviews, his mom certainly made it clear to
her friends that her sons would make their mark on the world
through their writing.

But back to fitness.  What is it?  Is it long-life?  Well,
mainly it's the ability to procreate.  Is it happiness? Uh
well... not exactly.

I think TK's meaning of life was to be happy.  He had an
idealistic vision that everyone in the world should be "free"
and "in control" of their life, and would therefore be...
happy.  But do people truly want to be free?  I pass again.

The manifesto definitely makes the point that most people are
unhappy or just "think" they are happy (but are just kidding
themselves and aren't really -- could this be???) and
meanwhile are running after goals to satisfy this vague sense
of dissatisfaction in their life which won't go away.

Let's pretend for the moment that one can measure a person's
happiness and come up with a single number (as silly as the
idea of an IQ) and heck, let's make the mean be 100 like it
is (supposed to be?) for IQ.

And let's also pretend that the happiness on the planet earth 
can be measured by adding up the happiness quotients of all
the *people* on the planet (people is important because TK clearly
puts people -- namely himself -- before other parts of nature).

Choices for world happiness of 10,000 units:

100 people * 100 HQ = 10,000 happiness units.
55.6 * 170 = 10,000 happiness units.

In other words:
Ted would rather have more individual happiness, and less
people. Unfortunately, the evolution says we will have more
and more people until we basically snuff ourselves out. (Gaia
hypothesis, Lynn Margoulis, etc) Evolution on the planet
earth will continue and there will be no more people
struggling with issues of power and control and happiness ---
no people at all.  Technology might delay this process by
increasing the carrying capacity of the earth, but it will
not go on for ever...

Some manifesto...

  How Some People Adjust

     77. Not everyone in industrial-technological society suffers from
     psychological problems. Some people even profess to be quite
     satisfied with society as it is. We now discuss some of the reasons
     why people differ so greatly in their response to modern society.

     78. First, there doubtless are differences in the strength of the
     drive for power. Individuals with a weak drive for power may have
     relatively little need to go through the power process, or at least
     relatively little need for autonomy in the power process. These are
     docile types who would have been happy as plantation darkies in the
     Old South. (We don't mean to sneer at "plantation darkies" of the
     Old South. To their credit, most of the slaves were NOT content with
     their servitude. We do sneer at people who ARE content with
     servitude.)
